title: Documents
outcome: Required traveller documents can be uploaded securely, reviewed by an authorized operator, corrected when needed and reflected truthfully in per-traveller readiness.
actor: Authenticated customer and an authorized operator user acting within the booking's operator scope.
modules: Documents owns document requirements, submission metadata, validation, review state and append-oriented review history.
Traveller supplies customer-owned traveller identities without duplicating identity data in Documents.
Booking supplies the confirmed booking and operator relationship used for resource authorization.
Private object storage holds encrypted document content behind short-lived authorized access.
routes: Document requirement -> Private upload -> Validation and quarantine
Authorized operator queue -> Safe document review
Per-traveller document state -> Derived booking readiness
acceptance: Document requirements come from an approved, explicit versioned policy and remain distinct per traveller and requirement.
Customers can upload only for account-owned travellers on eligible bookings, and operators can review only bookings within their authorized operator scope.
Objects remain private, encrypted and non-enumerable; access uses short-lived authorized URLs and every access is audited.
File size, declared type, content signature and malware status are validated before a reviewer can access a submission.
Unsafe or indeterminate uploads remain quarantined and produce a safe, actionable customer state.
Validation, under-review, approved, correction-required and rejected states are explicit and cannot be skipped by direct editing.
Resubmission preserves the prior submission and append-oriented review history, including actor, reason and timestamp.
Booking-level document readiness is derived only when every required traveller requirement is approved.
Document content, object keys and signed URLs never enter ordinary logs, analytics, integration events or customer-safe projections.
The approved retention and deletion schedule is enforced and auditable before production document storage is enabled.
Loading, empty, upload-progress, offline, validation, quarantine, permission, stale/conflict, correction, success and retry states are complete.
Customer and operator surfaces preserve approved NoorPath visual language and pass keyboard, focus, target-size, reflow, reduced-motion and WCAG checks.
exclusions: Visa lifecycle or official visa-authority decisions; owned by VS-13.
OCR, biometric matching, automated passport extraction or automated approval.
Permanent public document URLs, direct object-store listing or production documents in lower environments.
Changing the approved v1 requirements, retention schedule, private S3 access model or ClamAV fail-closed policy inside implementation.
General-purpose case management, CRM or unrestricted operator file browsing.
